item.title: Richer people have an edge when it comes to getting national park permits
item.description: Many outdoor enthusiasts have spent hours in front of a computer, racing to reserve a campsite, backpacking permit or national park entrance ticket. A recent study suggests that the way these reservation systems are designed can favor higher-income visitors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA's Curiosity rover catches stunning Martian dawn
item.description: A newly released panorama captured by NASA's Curiosity rover offers the most detailed view yet of distant, wind-carved Martian cliffs, highlighting features the mission's scientists have long been waiting to see up close. The scene was snapped at 8:30 a.m. local Mars time, showing striking blue hues in the foreground as bright morning light illuminates crags known as yardangs on the horizon. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Diet alone cannot explain differences in gut bacterial communities
item.description: Why do the gut microbiomes of people from industrialized and nonindustrialized regions differ? A study by the Helmholtz Center for Infection Research (HZI) in collaboration with the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), the University of Trento (Italy) and the University of Tübingen shows that diet alone does not explain these differences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reading beyond the peaks: Optical analysis decodes spectral complexity in twisted semiconductor layers
item.description: A study from the Research Center for Materials Nanoarchitectonics (MANA), one of the centers under the National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), presents a new method to reveal hidden material disorder reflected in complex photoluminescence spectra, paving the way for new optical diagnostics of material disorder in two-dimensional semiconductors and related light-emitting materials. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Viewing honey bee colonies as superorganisms could reshape beekeeping practices
item.description: A new study seeks to challenge the conventional view of a honey bee colony. Viewing colonies as superorganisms redefines the fundamental biology of the honey bee colony. These insights may have implications for modern beekeeping. Fuente: Phys.org.

The Sun is always rising somewhere. 🌄 On the 4,982nd Martian day of its mission, our Curiosity rover captured this photo of dawn breaking over distant... Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Meet the long-legged giants that light up the deep ocean
item.description: Thousands of meters below the waves off Australia's east coast, far beyond where sunlight can reach, a stunning light show takes place in the dark. The cause? Two species of long-legged creatures emitting a blue glow. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From food to fuel, AI helps pinpoint how to grow 'microalgae' at scale
item.description: Microalgae (microscopic organisms that use light and carbon dioxide to grow) can be used to make ingredients and food for animals, pigments and potentially renewable fuels. But growing microalgae efficiently at an industrial scale is difficult. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New chip-based frequency combs demonstrate potential for portable atomic clocks
item.description: The world would look radically different without rulers and measuring tapes that fit into a pocket. Carpenters, fashion designers and engineers rely on these trusty tools to check the size of everything from a wooden board to a fabric swatch. But physicists who work with light lack that same convenience for one of the basic measurements of their craft. They routinely need to measure and compare the frequencies—colors—of the light waves they are using. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How cultural background shapes our perception of dance
item.description: An international research team led by scientists from the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics (MPIEA) in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, conducted an in-depth study of our experiences when watching dance. The results show that our acculturation to a particular culture influences how we interpret emotions in a dance and perceive beauty and meaning in movement. This study comprises three publications in academic journals. The most recent publication was released in Perception. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tiny channels between plant cells respond to wound alerts through hydrogen peroxide bursts
item.description: When a person falls and gets a cut or a scrape, they often use hydrogen peroxide to clean the wound. This molecular compound is also produced within our cells, helping our immune system build its defenses against harmful bacteria or other pathogens. Hydrogen peroxide is produced inside plants, too, where it acts as a messenger, telling cells to beef up a plant's defenses when it is stressed, wounded or under attack. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How invasive Egyptian geese exploit food sources and carry parasites
item.description: The Egyptian goose, native to Africa, is considered an invasive species of Europe-wide significance. Researchers from the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Center and Goethe University Frankfurt spent four years investigating the ecological and economic impacts of its expansion. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stretching boosts thermal and electrical conductivity in new nanocomposite
item.description: A joint research team led by professors Seunghyun Baik and Joonmyung Choi from the School of Mechanical Engineering at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) has developed a new nanocomposite material whose electrical and thermal conductivities increase as it is stretched. The team successfully applied it to stable heat dissipation for foldable phones. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA to Cover Northrop Grumman CRS-24 Spacecraft Departure
item.description: After delivering more than 11,000 pounds of supplies, science experiments, and other cargo to the International Space Station for NASA, Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus XL spacecraft is scheduled to depart Friday, Oct. 9, as part of the company’s Commercial Resupply Services-24 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-24. Watch NASA’s live coverage of undocking and departure beginning at 12:30 […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Taveau

item.title: October 2026 Satellite Puzzler
item.description: Your challenge is to tell us the location of the satellite image and why it is interesting. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Lunar Grounding Challenge
item.description: As an astronaut traverses the lunar South Pole, tribocharging from walking on the lunar surface and plasma charging from the ambient plasma generate electric charge on the spacesuit. This problem is severely compounded when entering lunar shadows and Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs). In these dark zones, the spacesuit can buildup a substantial negative potential due […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Light

item.title: Blue-light labeling uncovers unexpected protein partners of folded DNA structures
item.description: DNA can be more than just a double helix. When four strands are folded into a compact bundle, they form a G-quadruplex (G4). These bundles form in guanine-rich regions across the genome, including telomeres at the ends of chromosomes and the control regions of genes, where the proteins that dock onto them help decide which genes are switched on. G4 does not act the same way everywhere. What it does depends on where it forms and which proteins bind to it. This is why understanding the interactions surrounding G4 is so important. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why older people value quiet spaces with people nearby
item.description: Older adults enjoy spending time in peaceful, green spaces, but not in complete isolation. For her Ph.D. research, Anne Grave investigated which characteristics are most important for the ideal living environment for people age 70 and older. Her findings show that relaxation occurs where tranquility, nature, safety and the presence of other people come together. By gathering input directly from older adults, she provides designers of public spaces with valuable insights into the needs of older residents. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists found a new magnetic mineral in Chang’e-6 Moon samples, preserved inside impact-glass particles
item.description: A groundbreaking discovery by researchers has unveiled a new magnetic mineral, γ-Fe, found in lunar samples from the Chang'e-6 mission. This remarkable find sheds light on the ancient magnetic environment of the Moon, now long lost. Detailed analysis of tiny iron particles within lunar impact glasses reveals that γ-Fe can maintain stable magnetic signals, potentially serving as a record of the Moon's magnetic history. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: What Europe's EU Inc. framework for boosting competitiveness can and should learn from startup fraud in the US
item.description: The European Parliament and the Council of the European Union are currently debating EU Inc., draft legislation seeking to establish a single set of rules for starting, operating and growing a business across EU member states. The proposed framework is designed to make business registration and operation within the EU faster, easier and more harmonized. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: El Niño and tropical Atlantic warming could offer early warning of extreme heat in the Amazon
item.description: El Niño and warming in the tropical Atlantic could help provide advance warning of extreme heat in the Amazon, with some signals appearing as much as seven months earlier, new research has found. Researchers from the ARC Center of Excellence for the Weather of the 21st Century and the National Institute of Space Research in Brazil studied how major patterns of natural climate variability influence temperature and rainfall extremes across the Amazon Basin. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Glenn Invites Phase 1 Proposals for Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory
item.description: NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland is seeking Phase 1 proposals for the design and construction of the Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory. The principal purpose of this procurement is to deliver a laboratory facility to support the testing and development of power systems, with associated site work, infrastructure, and systems. The laboratory will provide modern […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Gary Daines

item.title: A 2-in-1 approach captures toxic metals and recovers rare earth elements from wastewater
item.description: We generally throw away a broken camera lens, earphones or an old phone that has stopped working and is beyond repair because they seem useless when they no longer function. However, these objects contain rare earth elements (REEs) that have applications in magnets, superconductivity, optics and batteries, among others. When these objects end up in water, recovering REEs becomes difficult. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Let me explain': Corporate disclosures can take a circuitous route
item.description: The shortest distance between two points is a straight line, but sometimes taking the long way home can have advantages. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula's stellar jets
item.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope has unveiled numerous stars formerly hidden by clouds of dust in a stellar nursery known as NGC 7129—a cauldron of cosmic creation, 3,300 light-years from Earth. Webb captured infrared light, which pierces through the dense matter that scatters or absorbs other types of light. This region, rife with stellar objects in different stages of their lives, offers an opportunity to explore how stars shape their surroundings. Publicado también por: NASA, European Space Agency. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: El jefe de la NASA pide tener mente abierta ante el aumento de reportes de OVNIs: "Si hay algo, debemos estar"
item.description: Los OVNIs han cambiado de nombre, pero no de fama. Siguen teniendo muchas personas pendiente de ellos , tanto en el ámbito de lo esotérico como entre científicos y gobernantes. El Gobierno de Donald Trump se ha puesto como reto analizarlos a fondo. Por eso, a principios de este 2026 ordenó al Departamento de Guerra y a otras agencias identificar y publicar archivos del Gobierno sobre vida extraterrestre, fenómenos anómalos no identificados (UAP) y OVNIs. Ante esta situación, el actual administrador de la NASA, Jared Isaacman, ha insistido en que, si se descubre algo, su agencia debería… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: A gamma-ray burst's engine stayed active for nearly a month, breaking the previous record
item.description: Astronomers have observed the longest-lasting central engine activity ever recorded from a gamma-ray burst. The burst occurred at a redshift of 0.8577, and the activity lasted about 27 days in the burst's own rest frame—around 20 days longer than the previous record. The paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 18, explores different mechanisms that could be powering this puzzling burst. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Endangered Lantau toads show genetic and call differences that could signal an emerging species
item.description: The short-legged horned toad (Boulenophrys brachykolos), listed as endangered on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List of Threatened Species, is the only known small frog species in Hong Kong belonging to the genus Boulenophrys of the family Megophryidae. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: News you can use: Holiday travel does not have to break the bank
item.description: The holiday season is a time for getting together to celebrate, but if that get-together involves traveling by air, ticket prices may become a major barrier to holiday cheer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How gender shapes perceptions of workplace gossip
item.description: Workplace gossip is often viewed as negative, but research from The James & Gail Ellis School of Business Leadership has shown that it can play a more complex role in organizational relationships. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stem cells survive unexpectedly rough space travel
item.description: In early 2024, laboratory-grown neurospheres (i.e. clusters of neural stem cells) were sent to the International Space Station (ISS) to be exposed to microgravity. The return trip was delayed several times due to bad weather in the landing zone. As a result, the cells were outside controlled culture conditions for longer than anticipated—beyond the limit of what they were expected to survive. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ask the expert: What voters need to know about the rise of political deepfakes
item.description: Artificial intelligence is making it easier than ever to create convincing fake political content and harder to tell what's real. Now, a University of Missouri expert is helping voters navigate that changing information landscape ahead of this year's midterm elections. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Semana Mundial del Espacio 2026: este año se celebra la “Revolución de los Cohetes”
item.description: Esta edición busca incentivar los avances globales en ciencia y tecnología Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Unusual stars may not owe their origins to hypernovae after all
item.description: Evidence for hypernovae, theorized to be the most powerful explosions in the universe, has been disputed in two papers by University College London (UCL) researchers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Astronomers Solve Cosmic Cold Case with NASA Hubble Data
item.description: Diligent sleuthing by astronomers uncovered a surprising chemical clue that indicates the white dwarf star HS 0209+0832 may host a second-generation planet. This artist’s concept released on Oct. 5, 2026, depicts that possible explanation. The white dwarf is the “dead” core of a star that burned through all of its nuclear fuel and lost its outer […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Why is NASA bringing 7,500 contractors back to work as civil servants?
item.description: "The administrator's directive is a coherent and necessary vision for the future." Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Eric Berger

item.title: Heavy fermions emerge at an atomic-layer interface, unlocking new ways to design quantum materials
item.description: A research team led by the University of Osaka has directly observed, for the first time, an unusual heavy-fermion state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. Such states are closely linked to exotic quantum phenomena, including unconventional superconductivity, and the finding opens new possibilities for designing quantum materials through their interfaces. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Popular TikTok docs have big influence on Gen Z followers, new research finds
item.description: Young adults following physicians on TikTok consider them more accessible, credible and altruistic than their own doctors, even when the physician-influencers are selling products. Moreover, the followers haven't actually confirmed the influencers' medical credentials. Those are the main findings of a new study from Virginia Commonwealth University, co-authored by Suzanne Makarem, Ph.D., and published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Where are the best places for life in the cosmos? A universe in a supercomputer yields an answer
item.description: Earth seems like a troubled place right now, but at least our cosmic surroundings appear peaceful. This is not universally true, as explosions, collisions and other dangers lurk in other places and times. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: To keep GPS constellations from drifting, look to the moon
item.description: Global positioning systems are a key feature in everyday life for much of the world's population. Whether it's ensuring a ship delivers its goods safely or helping you avoid a road closure on your commute home, GPS can help. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: ESA at IAC 2026 – Day 2
item.description: International cooperation remained at the heart of ESA’s participation in the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, as ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher held a series of high-level meetings with partners from around the world. The exchanges reflected ESA’s commitment to strengthening existing partnerships while broadening cooperation with both established and emerging space actors. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Warming oceans reshape plankton, potentially leaving fish with less nutritious food
item.description: The world is changing. As humans, we tend to focus on what happens on land, but the planet's food systems depend on both terrestrial and marine ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A symbiotic marketplace: Gutless worms swap essential bacterial partners over time
item.description: A typical scene at a local farmers market: Various stalls offer fruit, vegetables and much more. Every customer has their favorite stalls, though these may change occasionally. Some symbiotic relationships seem to work just like that, a study by researchers from the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology reveals in Science Advances. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How political, cultural, and economic forces can shape the risk of zoonotic disease
item.description: In eastern Ethiopia, pressures like conflict and displacement are changing how people and their camels travel, shifting livestock into new environments and potentially influencing the risk of zoonotic diseases spreading between animals and humans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chinese team creates ‘lifelike’ hydrogel that changes shape for smart devices
item.description: Chinese researchers have developed a “lifelike” shape-changing hydrogel they say could provide a platform for next-generation developments, such as flexible tissue engineering scaffolds, brain-computer interfaces and humanlike robots. Inspired by living organisms, the team created a light-triggered system called STERS, which uses liquid metal particles to generate slow, self-sustaining chemical reactions that allow a hydrogel to change its structure over time. Capable of growing and changing... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela

item.title: Can a passing black hole disturbance leave a trace in Hawking radiation?
item.description: Black holes, despite their extreme nature, are described by surprisingly few basic parameters: their mass, charge and spin. Two black holes may have formed for completely different reasons and passed through very different histories, yet still end up in the same final state. John Wheeler summarized this idea with the famous phrase "black holes have no hair." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bacteria use collisions to navigate crowded environments, micro-maze experiments reveal
item.description: Some bacteria can sense when they bump into each other and use these interactions to shape how the group organizes and moves. This discovery reveals a new way microbes explore their environments using physical feedback rather than chemical signals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI chatbots may increase accurate political knowledge
item.description: As voters seeking information about political issues increasingly turn to LLMs to do research, will AI lead them astray with hallucinations and bias, distorting the democratic process? Maybe not, according to a study of AI use in the 2024 U.K. election, published in PNAS Nexus. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Molecular complexity as a signature of life
item.description: An abundance of complex molecules has been proposed as a universal signature of life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Colorectal cancer is rising in young people and often found too late
item.description: Colorectal cancer in young people is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, with researchers finding most patients age 21 or younger already had Stage III or IV disease. Because symptoms like rectal bleeding, weight loss, abdominal pain, and bowel changes may be overlooked, researchers are calling for greater vigilance. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Vanillin provides a sweet solution for chronic wound healing
item.description: A team from Flinders University's Biomedical Nanoengineering Laboratory has found that vanillin has pronounced antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties, making it a good candidate for wound-healing formulations. Their work is published in the International Journal of Pharmaceutics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fasting is a common practice, whether for religious reasons or with the goal of losing weight, preventing chronic disease, or even slowing aging. Those who fast for hea... Ver más
item.description: Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Goodbye joint replacements? Stanford scientists found a way to regrow cartilage and stop arthritis
item.description: Scientists have found a surprising way to regrow damaged knee cartilage by blocking a protein that becomes more abundant with age. In old mice, the treatment restored naturally lost cartilage and also helped prevent osteoarthritis after ACL-like knee injuries, while human cartilage taken from knee replacement patients began producing new, functional joint cartilage after exposure to the same inhibitor. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Blue light could cut food poisoning from raw chicken
item.description: A low-power blue light could be the key to significantly reducing food poisoning caused by raw chicken in the U.K., scientists at the University of Reading have found. Campylobacter is the most common cause of bacterial food poisoning worldwide. In the U.K. alone, there are hundreds of thousands of cases each year, costing an estimated £700 million annually in health care and lost productivity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Counting purpose and connection could reveal overlooked benefits of bike paths and parks
item.description: It's often the sight of heavy digging machinery that makes us question how our taxes and property taxes are being spent. As a new project begins, we may wonder why money is being spent on that and not on other things. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Webb Captures Commotion From Nebula’s Stellar Jets
item.description: A cauldron of cosmic creation is being revealed in a new image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. Webb has unveiled numerous stars formerly hidden by clouds of dust in a stellar nursery known as NGC 7129, which resides about 3,300 light-years from Earth. Stars, the engines of elemental creation, have life cycles that begin […] Publicado también por: European Space Agency. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Archaeologists may have finally solved a 100-year-old Florida mystery
item.description: Ancient pottery from Tampa Bay appears to have been made by migrant craftspeople who brought specialized Mississippian pottery-making knowledge hundreds of miles south. Remarkably, they even incorporated crushed fragments of older homeland pottery into new vessels, preserving a physical link to their past across generations. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: New report exposes modern poverty and inequality in one of Britain's 'most affluent cities'
item.description: The University of York's Cost of Living Research Group has examined modern living standards across the city and revealed the extent of hidden pockets of poverty and inequality in one of the North's most affluent cities. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
item.description: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Africa's rhinos often get the spotlight—but Indonesia's two rhino species are far closer to extinction
item.description: Small, hairy and cheekily charismatic. Those words sprang to mind when I first met a Sumatran rhinoceros (Dicerorhinus sumatrensis) after traversing the maze of wooden slat paths at the conservation center in the dense, humid forests of Malaysian Borneo. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: US, German scientists win Nobel medicine prize for work on light and brain
item.description: American Karl Deisseroth and Germans Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine ​on Monday for developing optogenetics, a technique that uses light to control individual nerve cells in the brain. Publicado también por: The Washington Post - World. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Physicists just saw quarks make waves in the Big Bang’s primordial soup
item.description: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have captured the clearest evidence yet that quark-gluon plasma, the scorching-hot matter that filled the newborn universe, behaves like a true liquid. By tracking individual quarks as they blasted through the plasma, researchers saw them leave behind ripples, splashes, and swirling wakes much like a duck moving through water. The finding suggests this primordial “soup” is so dense that it can slow speeding quarks and respond collectively as a fluid. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Yosemite's meadows can be restored, but it will take time and effort
item.description: Researchers at Colorado State University are leading an attempt to restore Yosemite National Park's iconic meadows before it's too late by reintroducing native plants that once covered the landscape. Results are published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Un pueblo zamorano de 180 habitantes quería decorar sus calles así que sus vecinas tejieron 15 metros de ganchillo
item.description: El ganchillo (el de verdad, no el de la IA ) siempre fue un pasatiempo de calma y tiempo libre. Salvo cuando un pueblo entero se junta y decide convertirlo en parte de la festividad. Si en tu pueblo la fiesta empieza con traca y cohetes, en Losacino de Alba, en la zamorana Tierra de Alba, la fiesta empezó con una aguja. Del 2 al 4 de octubre, por la Virgen del Rosario, sus calles se vistieron con 20 hilos, más de 150 metros de cuerda y unos 300 banderines de ganchillo , muchos de mandalas y espirales. Las vecinas los tejieron durante meses y los jóvenes los colgaron. Cómo se teje una fiesta… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Isra Fdez

item.title: One simple addition to postpartum care made a major difference
item.description: New mothers paired with patient navigators were much more likely to receive postpartum care, depression screening, preventive testing, and ongoing primary care. By helping with barriers such as transportation, childcare, scheduling, and confusing medical information, navigators may provide a powerful way to improve women’s long-term health. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 'Ghost particles' from space telescope wins physics Nobel
item.description: Belgian physicist Prof Francis Halzen has won for his pioneering work on an observatory that detects particles from space. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Cancer survival is improving, but return‑to‑work support is falling behind
item.description: Australia has made significant strides in improving cancer survival, but new research from Griffith University finds far less progress in supporting survivors' return to work, which remains a major challenge for many. The industry research report, "Return-to-Work for Cancer Survivors in the Life Insurance Context," was a joint research collaboration between Griffith University and Hannover Life Re of Australasia Ltd. and was published in the Griffith Research Repository. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX desafía décadas de superstición de la NASA y lanza con éxito una misión tripulada con el número 13
item.description: Las supersticiones pueden arraigarse muchísimo con el paso de los años. Igual que la supuesta muerte de Molière tras vestir de amarillo en una representación teatral en 1673 ha llevado a que hoy en día nadie use ese color en los escenarios, la explosión de un tanque de oxígeno en la nave del Apolo 13 condujo a que ninguna misión estadounidense llevase como apellido ese número de mal agüero. Al menos no hasta ahora, pues la misión Crew-13 de SpaceX lo ha lucido sin miedo y ha llegado a su destino con éxito. Rápidos y superando miedos . Desde lo ocurrido con el Apolo 13, la carrera espacial… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: New report reveals gaps in corporate modern slavery disclosures
item.description: Many of Australia's largest companies fail to show enough public evidence that workers affected by modern slavery can safely report concerns, a new Monash University–led report has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
item.description: China’s booming artificial intelligence sector has given local researchers good reason to remain in the country, but it has yet to lure overseas scientists despite a government push. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Zeyi Yang

item.title: Nature's capacity to 'bounce back' when species are lost is vastly overestimated, global analysis finds
item.description: The idea that ecosystems carry plenty of backup, so if a small number of species become extinct there is little harm, has been greatly overestimated, according to the largest global study of its kind. Publicado también por: Hacker News - Portada. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Watch Sophie Adenot return to Earth
item.description: On 7 October 2026, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot and her Crew-12 crewmates will undock from the International Space Station at around 12:05 GMT/14:05 CEST to begin their journey back to Earth. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: European rover trains for Mars in the desert
item.description: For eight days, a Mars rover prototype travelled 220 metres across a barren landscape, following commands from a science team some 1200 kilometres away. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Scientists finally see how nature moves energy so efficiently
item.description: Researchers have captured key steps in a chemical reaction that helps nature transfer energy with remarkable efficiency. Ultrafast X-rays revealed how changes involving electrons and protons are closely linked to the rearrangement of surrounding water molecules. Because similar reactions drive photosynthesis and other energy-conversion processes, the technique could help scientists develop better catalysts, fuel cells, and flow batteries. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

Claimed at various times to be a book in a lost language, a musical score, an instruction manual or just an elaborate hoax, the so-called Voynich manuscript’s true meaning has defied cryptographers and codebreakers for centuries. item.description: The Nobel medicine prize was awarded Monday to US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and German scientists Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their pioneering work in the neuroscience field of optogenetics. item.description: Predatory wasps are hijacking shelters built by tropical trees for their ant defenders, potentially disrupting an ancient partnership that protects the plants from hungry insects. item.title: Exploring systemic racism as the default explanation for disparities
item.description: Much of the field of sociology treats systemic racism as its default explanation for racial disparities rather than as an open question that requires further investigation and evidence, according to a recent position paper. The assumptions and moralization surrounding the origins of race-based disparities have undermined the discipline and made it difficult—and professionally costly—to challenge the concept, says author Ilana Redstone, a professor of sociology at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Neutrons, rotating black holes, and a galactic PeVatron at the center of the Milky Way
item.description: Galactic black holes are cosmic mitochondria, powerhouses of the universe. Most of the energy these supermassive black holes produce comes from the material surrounding them: superheated plasma in their accretion disks interacting with tremendous magnetic fields. But there is a more direct way to extract energy from a black hole. It's known as the Penrose process, and a new study asks whether we could discover a signature of this process. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: MIT scientists find a hidden cancer risk of the keto diet
item.description: A ketogenic diet increased small-intestinal tumors in cancer-prone mice while reducing tumors in the colon, revealing a strikingly different response within neighboring parts of the gut. Researchers traced the increased risk not to ketones, but to the way intestinal stem cells processed the diet’s high levels of fat. That fat-burning activity pushed the cells to multiply more rapidly, potentially raising the chance of cancerous changes. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 26 mil reproducciones · 330 reacciones | Nos EUA - Um brasileiro de 46 anos foi preso no último domingo (4) após aparecer vestido como um agente do Serviço de Imigração e Controle de Alfândegas dos Estados Unidos (ICE, na sigla em inglês) em um local de votação das eleições brasileiras Miami, na Flórida. ➡️​ Segundo o gabinete do xerife do condado de Miami-Dade, Danilo Silva circulava pelo campus de Kendall do Miami Dade College, onde brasileiros votavam, usando boné e jaqueta com identificação do ICE, óculos escuros, máscara cobrindo o rosto e botas táticas. De acordo com o relatório policial, ele caminhava pelos locais de votação e abordava pessoas na intenção de causar medo entre os eleitores. A NBC filmou o momento da prisão. Após receber as denúncias, agentes uniformizados e investigadores à paisana passaram a monitorar a área. Em determinado momento, Silva foi confrontado por dois homens, um deles filmando a situação. Os envolvidos iniciaram uma discussão, e os investigadores intervieram. Questionado pelos policiais, Silva admitiu que não era agente federal. Segundo o relato, ele afirmou que as roupas eram uma "fantasia" comprada pela internet, na Amazon. Ainda de acordo com as autoridades, o homem disse que havia comparecido ao local para votar usando uma camisa da seleção brasileira. Depois, retornou ao carro, trocou de roupa e vestiu o uniforme semelhante ao utilizado por agentes do ICE. Aos investigadores, Silva afirmou que queria apenas "ver a reação das pessoas". ➡️​ Ele foi preso em flagrante. Segundo o relatório da polícia, durante a abordagem, ele ficou exaltado e ameaçou um dos investigadores, dizendo que ele se arrependeria da decisão de prendê-lo. Segundo o Miami Herald, em seguida, Silva tentou subornar os policiais para ser liberado. De acordo com o jornal, ele ofereceu dinheiro e disse que poderia mostrar a transferência pelo celular. Ele foi levado para o centro de detenção Turner Guilford Knight. Ele foi acusado de intimidação de eleitores, tentativa de suborno, uso ilegal de insígnias das forças de segurança e conduta desordeira. Saiba mais no #g1. #ice #brasileiro #estadosunidos #notícias #g1mundo | g1 - O Portal de Notícias da globo
